title: Tigrayan Himbasha
community: Tigray region — the celebration bread of the north
author: Mama Tigist
desc: Tigrayan Himbasha — the round, decorated celebration bread of the Tigray region, pan-baked with nigella seeds and fenugreek. Distinct from Amhara Ambasha — the Tigrayan version uses nigella seeds (black cumin) as the signature spice, giving it a distinctive bitter-aromatic character.
longDesc: Tigrayan Himbasha is the northern version of the Ethiopian celebration bread — pan-baked, circular, decorated with geometric patterns, and fragrant with the nigella seeds that are the Tigrayan signature spice.
steps: Dissolve yeast in water with sugar. Rest 10 minutes.
Combine flour, salt, nigella seeds, and fenugreek.
Add yeast mixture and oil. Knead 8 minutes.
Press into a large round (2cm thick). Score decorative pattern.
Cook in a flat pan covered on medium-low: 20 minutes per side.
chefTips: Nigella seeds are the Tigrayan Himbasha signature — do not substitute.
The decorative pattern is as important as the flavour.
commonMistakes: Omitting nigella seeds — makes it Ambasha, not Himbasha.
cookingScience: See ETH005 for Ambasha science. Nigella seeds contain thymoquinone — an antioxidant that is released during baking.
sustainabilityTips: Tigrayan nigella seeds from the highland farms.
culturalNote: Tigrayan Himbasha is the bread of the ancient north — pan-baked in the same way in the same mountains that produced the Aksumite civilisation and the first Ethiopian Christians. The nigella seeds that mark it are the northern signature.
